reference_answer: The backend currently stores runs in a thread-safe InMemoryRunStore; a backend restart loses them. The desktop API resolves a local Tauri backend URL, starts a run, polls snapshots and opens an event stream; the Lit component holds its current run in instance state, which a desktop restart loses. A sound plan gives the backend authoritative durable run/event storage and a stable run ID, plus a desktop-side local pointer or discovery mechanism to reconnect. Compare storing an active run pointer in desktop state versus backend-side listing/discovery, define queued/running/succeeded/failed and clarification transitions, last-event replay, crash semantics and migration from in-memory runs. Validate with restart and duplicate-submission tests; roll back without fabricating completion.

Local backend URL may be rediscovered after restart.

ambiguities: Recovering a pointer without backend persistence is insufficient.
An in-progress call may be unknown after a backend crash.

acceptable_alternatives: A staged plan that first makes terminal results durable before live-run resume is acceptable.
